facts.claim: EO 14380 declared a national emergency with respect to Cuba and created an additional-tariff mechanism tied to countries supplying oil to Cuba.
visualNotAllowed: specific supplier country unless separately sourced

facts.claim: EO 14389 ended additional tariffs imposed under IEEPA, including those associated with EO 14380, while leaving the underlying emergency and non-tariff actions in place.
visualNotAllowed: depicting January tariffs as unchanged through the full year

facts.claim: EO 14404 expanded sanctions authorities related to Cuba and delegated implementation functions to the Secretary of State and Secretary of the Treasury.
visualAllowed: authentic Rubio still/video as Secretary of State
visualNotAllowed: Rubio presented as sole author of the sanctions regime

facts.claim: OFAC added multiple Cuba-related individuals and entities to the SDN list, including ICAP and MINFAR.
visualNotAllowed: asserting unverified criminal conduct beyond the official attributed rationale
facts.attribution: fact for designation; rationale attributed to US government

facts.claim: OFAC designated Banco Exterior de Cuba and additional Cuba-related targets under EO 14404.
visualNotAllowed: fabricated bank failure or customer footage

facts.claim: OFAC updated Cuba-related restrictions affecting indirect transactions with Cuba Restricted List entities and removed the U-turn authorization in the September regulatory changes.
visualNotAllowed: claiming all Cuba transactions became prohibited

facts.claim: Marco Rubio served as Secretary of State and was a public voice and implementing official for parts of the Cuba policy, but did not personally sign the presidential executive orders.
facts.source: State Department + White House executive orders
visualNotAllowed: Rubio depicted as sole author of all measures
